title: K, kh, and g: כּ כ ך ק ג
topic: כּ (k) and כ ך (kh); ק (k); ג (g)
why: Start of the second unit: the sounds k, kh and g, with the letter כ that changes its sound depending on the dot, and the final ך. You can finally read מָה שְׁלוֹמְךָ, and you discover that the adjective comes after the noun.

{"lessons": ["

K, kh and g: five new forms

LetterNameSound
כּkafk (with the dot)
כkhafkh (without the dot)
ךfinal khafkh, at the end of a word
קkufk
גgimelg, always hard as in \"go\"

The kh sound doesn't exist in English: it's a raspy breath from the back of the throat, like the ch in Scottish \"loch\" or German \"Bach\". It's a bit like the throaty Hebrew r, only with more friction.

מֶלֶךְmelekh: king

ג is always read g, never j as in \"gem\": גְּלִידָה is read glida (ice cream), not \"jlida\".

", "

Two k's, two kh's

Like בּ / ב, the letter kaf changes its sound depending on the dot: כּ = k, כ = kh. And ק also makes k: כֶּלֶב (kelev, dog) and קָר (kar, cold) start with the same sound. Only the spelling tells them apart, like \"c\" and \"k\" in English (cat, kit): learn each word with its letter.

The final ך is always read kh. Sometimes it carries a kamats: לְךָ is read lekha (to you, to a man); לָךְ is read lakh (to you, to a woman). You can finally read מָה שְׁלוֹמְךָ? and מָה שְׁלוֹמֵךְ?.

תּוֹדָה לְךָ! / תּוֹדָה לָךְ!Thank you! (lit. thanks to you; to a man / to a woman) [toda lekha! / toda lakh!]

A famous exception: in כָּל הַכָּבוֹד (well done!), כָּל is read kol, not \"kal\". You'll hear it often in the app!

", "

Big, cold, here

The adjective goes AFTER the noun, and it agrees: כֶּלֶב גָּדוֹל (a big dog), כַּלְבָּה גְּדוֹלָה (a big female dog). Still no verb \"to be\": הַכֶּלֶב גָּדוֹל, the dog is big.

כָּאן קָר.It's cold here. [kan kar]
מָה קוֹרֶה?What's new? [ma kore?]
גַּם אֲנִי בַּגַּן.Me too, I'm at the park. [gam ani ba-gan]

After הַ (the), the next letter usually takes a dot (not א or ר: הָאִישׁ): so הַכֶּלֶב is read ha-kelev, with a k. גַּן is the garden, the park… and also kindergarten!
